title: Microsoft 365 & Office
blurb: Word, Excel, PowerPoint: activation, sign-in, crashes, files that won't open.

remedies.title: Office says "Unlicensed product" or "Product deactivated"
remedies.why: Office can't confirm your licence: you're signed in with a different account, the subscription lapsed, or the licence check is stale.

steps.text: In Word, open File › Account (Mac: Word › Sign In) and check the account shown is the one with the subscription.
Sign out, close every Office app, open Word and sign in again with the licensed account.
Check the subscription at account.microsoft.com/services (home) or ask IT (work).
Check the date and time are correct; activation fails with a wrong clock.
Repair Office: Settings › Apps › Microsoft 365 › Modify › Online Repair.

remedies.escalate: At work, IT has to assign you a licence; tell them the account shown in File › Account.

remedies.title: Microsoft 365 sign-in loops or shows an error code
remedies.why: The work account's device registration or saved sign-in is damaged, or your organisation's rules (like MFA or a compliant device) aren't met.

steps.text: Note the error code; it tells IT exactly what failed.
Check "Access work or school" shows your account; if it shows an error, choose Disconnect only if IT agrees, then reconnect.
Remove saved Office sign-ins: Credential Manager › Windows Credentials › entries starting with MicrosoftOffice16 or ADAL.
Delete Microsoft Office identity entries in Keychain Access (search "Microsoft Office Identities"), then reopen Office.
Check the clock is correct.
Try signing in at office.com in a private browser window; if that fails too, the account itself needs IT.

remedies.escalate: Give IT the error code, time, and whether office.com works.

remedies.title: Office apps crash or behave strangely (repair Office)
remedies.why: Damaged program files or a broken update. Repair puts Office back without touching your documents.

steps.text: Close all Office apps.
Settings › Apps › Installed apps › Microsoft 365 (or Office) › ⋯ › Modify › Quick Repair. If that doesn't help, run Online Repair (downloads Office again, ~30 minutes).
Start the app in safe mode (hold Ctrl while opening it); if it works there, turn off add-ins in File › Options › Add-ins.
Install Office updates: open Word › File › Account › Update Options › Update Now.

remedies.title: Word or Excel crashes when opening one file
remedies.why: That file is damaged or contains something (a macro, a link, an image) the app chokes on.

steps.text: Open it with File › Open › select the file › the arrow next to Open › Open and Repair (Windows Office).
Open it in Word/Excel on the web (upload to OneDrive) and save a fresh copy from there.
Look for an older copy: OneDrive/SharePoint › Version history, or File Explorer › right-click › Restore previous versions.
Look for an older copy: OneDrive/SharePoint › Version history, or Time Machine.

remedies.title: I lost a document I didn't save
remedies.why: Office keeps AutoRecover copies every few minutes, and AutoSave keeps files in OneDrive saved as you type.

steps.text: Open the app again: a Document Recovery panel often appears on the left.
Word › File › Info › Manage Document › Recover Unsaved Documents (Excel: Recover Unsaved Workbooks).
Look in ~/Library/Containers/com.microsoft.Word/Data/Library/Preferences/AutoRecovery (Finder › Go › Go to Folder).
If the file was ever saved to OneDrive or SharePoint, open Version history there.
From now on keep files in OneDrive with AutoSave on (switch at the top left).

remedies.title: "File is locked for editing by another user"
remedies.why: Someone (sometimes you, on another computer) has it open, or Office left a lock behind after a crash.

steps.text: Ask the named person to close it. If it names you, close it on your other devices.
Save files on OneDrive/SharePoint and use co-authoring so several people can edit at once.
If it's left over from a crash, restart the computer; for a network folder, a hidden file starting with ~$ next to it can be deleted once nobody has it open.

remedies.title: Excel is slow, "Calculating" or "Not responding"
remedies.why: Large sheets with many formulas, whole-column references, volatile functions (like NOW, INDIRECT, OFFSET) or lots of formatting.

steps.text: Set Formulas › Calculation Options › Manual while editing, then press F9 to recalculate.
Replace references to whole columns (A:A) with real ranges, and remove unused rows/columns of formatting.
Save as .xlsb (binary workbook) for very large files; it opens faster.
Close other workbooks and turn off add-ins you don't need.

remedies.title: "Microsoft has blocked macros" in a file
remedies.why: Office blocks macros in files from the internet or email, because they're a common way to spread malware.

steps.text: Only use macros in files you expected from someone you trust.
If you trust it, save the file, right-click it › Properties › tick Unblock › OK, then open it again.
Better: keep trusted macro files in a Trusted Location your IT sets up.

remedies.escalate: At work, IT controls macro settings; ask them rather than changing security options.

remedies.title: Update Office
remedies.why: Office updates fix bugs and security holes; many problems go away after updating.

steps.text: Open Word › File › Account › Update Options › Update Now.
Open Word › Help › Check for Updates (Microsoft AutoUpdate), or update through the App Store if installed from there.

remedies.title: OneNote won't sync
remedies.why: The notebook lost its connection or sign-in, or one section has a conflict.

steps.text: File › Info › View Sync Status › Sync All (Windows), or Notebooks › right-click › Sync This Notebook (Mac).
Open the notebook on OneNote for the web; if changes are there, the problem is this app.
Sign out of OneNote and back in.
Copy pages out of a section that won't sync into a new section.

remedies.title: Document looks different or fonts are missing
remedies.why: The document uses a font this computer doesn't have, so another one stands in and changes the layout.

steps.text: Ask the sender which font they used, or for a PDF copy if you only need to read or print it.
Install the font (double-click the font file › Install).
In Word, File › Options › Save › Embed fonts in the file, before sending documents with unusual fonts.
Check Font Book for disabled or duplicate fonts.

remedies.title: An Office add-in or tab disappeared
remedies.why: Office turns off add-ins that crash or slow it down, and they can be removed by updates.

steps.text: File › Options › Add-ins › Manage: Disabled Items › Go, re-enable it, restart the app.
File › Options › Add-ins › Manage: COM Add-ins › Go, tick it.
In Outlook, the Teams Meeting button returns after signing in to Teams and restarting Outlook.
